mainTopic: Who is exempt from ראייה, and which money and which days may be used for Festival offerings and for שמחה
overview: The amud opens with אביי rejecting a suggested reading of the פסוק 'כל זכורך', that a father must bring all his sons up together. He says that point is obvious. So the גמרא says the פסוק teaches the rule of אחרים: workers whose jobs make them smell bad, like a dung-gatherer, a copper smelter and a tanner, are exempt from ראייה, because others avoid them. A new משנה then teaches that Festival עולות come from חולין money, while שלמים may come from מעשר שני money. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the חגיגה of the first day of פסח. The משנה also lists which meat offerings let ישראלים and כהנים fulfill שמחה, and it excludes birds and meal-offerings. The גמרא finds the משנה's wording problematic: it seems either to allow מעשר for עולות on יום טוב or to follow בית שמאי. It answers that words are missing. Voluntary עולות come only on חול המועד, while the required עולת ראייה comes even on יום טוב but only from חולין. A ברייתא confirms this, and רב אשי explains that the dispute covers only the חגיגה of the fifteenth, not the fourteenth.

steps.title: אביי rejects the idea that the verse is needed for a father of many sons
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is no need for a פסוק to teach that a father must bring all his sons together. It is obvious, because you could not make some of them late and others early.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That is obvious! Which of the sons would you make into lazy sinners, and which of them would you make into eager ones?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against the earlier suggestion about what 'כל זכורך' teaches. He says that idea is obvious, so a פסוק is not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier suggestion said the פסוק teaches that all the sons go up together. אביי argues that common sense already says this. A father cannot pick one son to look lazy by going later and another to look eager by going first. If the lesson is obvious, the פסוק must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so no source is needed
Negligent people, sinners (here: those who go up late)
Eager, quick people who do the מצוה at the first chance
You make, you turn someone into

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: That is obvious;
which of them would you make into sinners,
phrases.notes: The son who goes up on a later day would look lazy for not coming at the first chance.

phrases.english: and which of them would you make into eager ones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of 'כל זכורך' proposed just before this section
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק to teach that all of a man's sons go up together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That lesson is obvious from common sense, so a פסוק would not be needed for it

steps.title: So what does the verse come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the earlier reading has been rejected, the גמרא asks what the פסוק 'כל זכורך' is really teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for what purpose does the verse come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what lesson 'כל זכורך' teaches now that the first idea is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word of the תורה teaches something. Since the 'many sons' reading is obvious, it needs a new, real lesson for the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק (verse)
What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: Rather, the verse, for what does it come?
phrases.notes: The verse here is 'כל זכורך', all your males.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from אביי's rejection: a new purpose for the פסוק is needed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק 'כל זכורך' actually teaches

steps.title: The verse teaches that people with foul-smelling jobs are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches the rule of אחרים. A dung-gatherer, a copper smelter and a tanner are exempt from ראייה, because they cannot go up together with all the other men.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches what אחרים taught. As a ברייתא says: אחרים say: a dung-gatherer, a copper smelter and a tanner are exempt from appearing at the בית המקדש. As it says, 'all your males,' meaning someone who is able to go up with all your males. These people are excluded, since they cannot go up with all your males.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'כל זכורך' is the source for אחרים's ruling. Workers whose jobs leave them smelling bad are exempt from ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all your males' are read as 'one who can go up together with everyone.' Other people avoid these workers because of the smell, so they cannot join the crowd. That is why they are left out of the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a name for an unnamed תנא (often said to be רבי מאיר)
One who gathers dung for tanning hides
One who smelts and refines copper
A tanner of hides
The מצוה of appearing at the בית המקדש on the רגל

steps.whatToRemember: 'כל זכורך' teaches that a man must be able to go up together with everyone else. People whose jobs make them smell bad, like the dung-gatherer, copper smelter and tanner, are exempt from ראייה.

phrases.english: For that which Acherim taught.
As it is taught: Acherim say:
A dung-gatherer, a copper smelter, and a tanner
are exempt from appearing,
as it is said: "all your males,"

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת עִם כׇּל זְכוּרְךָ.
phrases.english: one who is able to go up with all your males.
These are excluded,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לַעֲלוֹת עִם כׇּל זְכוּרְךָ.
phrases.english: since they cannot go up with all your males.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches אחרים's exemption for workers whose jobs keep them from going up together with everyone

steps.title: משנה: burnt-offerings from plain money, peace-offerings from tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that עולות brought on חול המועד must be bought with חולין money. שלמים may be bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Burnt-offerings brought on the intermediate days of the Festival must come from non-sacred money, and the peace-offerings may come from tithe money.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on which money may be used to pay for the Festival offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely and must be paid for with plain חולין money. שלמים are mostly eaten by the owner, so they may be bought with מעשר שני money, which is meant for eating in ירושלים anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Burnt-offerings, burned completely on the מזבח
Plain, non-sacred property or money
Peace-offerings, mostly eaten by the owners
Here: מעשר שני money, spent on food in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעשר' here means מעשר שני money, not מעשר בהמה (animal tithe), which comes up later in this משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Burnt-offerings on the intermediate days of the Festival
come from non-sacred money,
and the peace-offerings from the tithe.
phrases.notes: This means the money a person used to redeem his מעשר שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עוֹלוֹת בַּמּוֹעֵד בָּאוֹת מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Festival עולות must come from חולין money; שלמים may come from מעשר שני money

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the first day of פסח
steps.stepSummary: For the offering of the first day of פסח, בית שמאי require חולין money. בית הלל allow מעשר money.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day of פסח, בית שמאי say it must come from non-sacred money, and בית הלל say it may come from tithe money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה records an argument about the offering brought on the first יום טוב of פסח. The question is whether it may be paid for with מעשר money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 allowed שלמים in general to come from מעשר money. Here בית שמאי make the first day of פסח stricter and require חולין. בית הלל keep the usual rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The first festival day of פסח
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל

phrases.english: On the first day of Pesach,
Beit Shammai say: from non-sacred money,
and Beit Hillel say: from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed special case to the general rule about שלמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: חולין only; בית הלל: מעשר money is allowed

steps.title: How ordinary Jews fulfill their duty of rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: ישראלים fulfill their duty of eating meat on the Festival with vowed or donated offerings and with מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Israelites fulfill their obligation with vowed and donated offerings and with the animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the duty of שמחה, rejoicing by eating meat. It lists which offerings let a regular Jew fulfill that duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person does not need a special new offering for שמחה. Any שלמים he eats on the Festival counts, whether he vowed it, donated it, or it is מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfill their obligation
Vowed offerings ('I take on myself to bring')
Donated offerings ('this animal is an offering')
The animal tithe, eaten by its owner

phrases.english: Israelites fulfill their obligation
phrases.notes: This is the duty of שמחה, rejoicing by eating offering meat on the Festival.

phrases.english: with vowed and donated offerings
and with the animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the rules for שמחה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראלים fulfill שמחה with נדרים, נדבות and מעשר בהמה

steps.title: How כהנים fulfill rejoicing, and what does not count
steps.stepSummary: כהנים fulfill their duty of rejoicing with their portions of חטאות, אשמות, בכור, and the breast and thigh of שלמים. Birds and meal-offerings do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the priests fulfill it with sin-offerings, guilt-offerings, the firstborn, and the breast and thigh. But not with birds, and not with meal-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the offerings that count for the כהנים' שמחה. It ends by excluding birds and meal-offerings for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים receive meat from offerings that ordinary people do not eat, so those portions count for their שמחה. Birds and מנחות are left out, because only animal meat counts as rejoicing.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings, whose meat the כהנים eat
Guilt-offerings, whose meat the כהנים eat
A firstborn animal, given to the כהן
The breast and thigh of שלמים, the כהן's portion
Meal-offerings made of flour

steps.whatToRemember: שמחה on the Festival needs animal meat. ישראלים use their own שלמים and מעשר בהמה, and כהנים use their priestly portions. Birds and meal-offerings never count.

phrases.english: And the priests with sin-offerings and guilt-offerings
and with the firstborn, and with the breast and thigh.
But not with birds, and not with meal-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching list for כהנים and adds what is excluded
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים fulfill שמחה with חטאות, אשמות, בכור, and חזה ושוק; birds and מנחות do not count

steps.title: Does the משנה imply that עולות on the Festival day may come from מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's ruling about burnt-offerings on חול המועד. If they come from חולין on the intermediate days, then on יום טוב they would seem to come from מעשר. But that is impossible, since an obligatory offering must come from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But then the burnt-offerings that come from non-sacred money are the ones brought on the intermediate days. That means on יום טוב itself they may come from מעשר! Why? An עולה is an obligation, and anything obligatory may only come from non-sacred money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reading the exact words of the משנה and finds that they seem to lead to an impossible conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה linked 'from חולין' specifically to עולות on the intermediate days. That suggests that on יום טוב the rule is different, meaning מעשר would be allowed. But the עולת ראייה is a required offering, and a required offering may never be paid for with מעשר שני money, so the implied reading clashes with a basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Here: the intermediate days of the Festival (חול המועד)
Ordinary, non-sacred money or property
Here: מעשר שני money, which belongs in ירושלים
Something a person is obligated to bring

phrases.english: GEMARA: But then: burnt-offerings during the intermediate days
are the ones that come from non-sacred money,
which implies that on the Festival day they come from מעשר?
Why? It is an obligatory matter!
And any obligatory matter
may come only from non-sacred money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עוֹלוֹת — בַּמּוֹעֵד הוּא דְּבָאוֹת מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה's ruling from Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase that עולות on the intermediate days come from חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that on יום טוב they may come from מעשר. That contradicts the rule that an obligatory offering comes only from חולין.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as banning עולות on יום טוב would follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that perhaps the משנה means עולות are brought only on חול המועד and not on יום טוב at all. It rejects this, because that view belongs to בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה is teaching that עולות are brought on the intermediate days but not on יום טוב, whose opinion is that? בית שמאי's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible rescue for the משנה and immediately knocks it down as matching only בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading would avoid the מעשר problem, because there would simply be no עולות on יום טוב. But a סתם משנה should not follow בית שמאי, whose view is not the הלכה, so this reading creates a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible answer
This is what it teaches us
According to whom?
The Festival day itself, when work is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
phrases.english: And if you would say: this is what it teaches us
that burnt-offerings may come on the intermediate days,
but on the Festival day they do not come at all,
then whose view is it? בית שמאי's?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects a possible reading that would avoid the problem raised in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reading that the משנה forbids עולות on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That position is בית שמאי's, and an anonymous משנה is not expected to follow them.

steps.title: The משנה showing that בית שמאי forbid עולות on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה as the source. בית שמאי allow שלמים on יום טוב without סמיכה but forbid עולות. בית הלל allow both, with סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: בית שמאי say one brings שלמים but does not lean hands on them, and does not bring עולות. בית הלל say one brings שלמים and עולות, and leans hands on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that banning עולות on יום טוב is בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה shows that only בית שמאי forbid עולות on יום טוב, while בית הלל allow them. So the reading suggested in Step 9 really does match בית שמאי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)
Peace-offerings, which are mostly eaten by the owners
Burnt-offerings, which are burned entirely on the altar

phrases.english: As we learned: בית שמאי say:
One brings peace-offerings but does not lean hands on them,
but not burnt-offerings.
And בית הלל say:
One brings peace-offerings and burnt-offerings,
and one leans hands on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: That forbidding עולות on יום טוב is בית שמאי's position
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in ביצה recording the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: gift-type עולות versus the required עולת ראייה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fills in the missing words. Gift-type עולות from vows and donations come only on חול המועד. The required עולת ראייה comes even on יום טוב, but only from חולין. Then come the rulings on שלמי שמחה and the Pesach חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches. Burnt-offerings from vows and donations come on the intermediate days, not on יום טוב. The burnt-offering of appearance comes even on יום טוב, but only from non-sacred money. Peace-offerings of rejoicing may come even from מעשר. For the חגיגה of the first day of פסח, בית שמאי say it comes from חולין and בית הלל say it may come from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both problems by saying the משנה has words missing, and it reads the משנה with those words filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'only on חול המועד' applies to gift-type עולות, which are not a holiday need. That fits even בית הלל. The rule 'only from חולין' applies to the required עולת ראייה, which may be brought even on יום טוב. So no עולה is ever paid for with מעשר, and the משנה is no longer forced to follow בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words
Vowed and donated offerings, which are voluntary rather than required
The required burnt-offering for appearing at the בית המקדש on the Festival
Peace-offerings eaten to rejoice on the Festival
The Festival peace-offering

steps.whatToRemember: Gift-type עולות are not brought on יום טוב itself. The required עולת ראייה is brought even on יום טוב, but always from חולין, because required offerings can never come from מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different kinds of עולות here. 'Only on חול המועד' refers to voluntary עולות. 'Only from חולין' refers to the required עולת ראייה.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Burnt-offerings of vows and donations
come on the intermediate days,
but on the Festival day they do not come.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה בָּאָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And the burnt-offering of appearance comes even on the Festival day,
and when it comes,
it comes only from non-sacred money.

phrases.aramaic: וְשַׁלְמֵי שִׂמְחָה בָּאִין אַף מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: And peace-offerings of rejoicing may come even from מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲגִיגַת יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: And the Festival offering of the first day of פסח:
בית שמאי say: from non-sacred money,
and בית הלל say: from מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of Steps 8 and 9 by filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed either to allow מעשר for עולות on יום טוב or to follow בית שמאי in forbidding עולות on יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: Voluntary עולות come only on חול המועד. The required עולת ראייה comes even on יום טוב, but only from חולין.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rules
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches the filled-in משנה from Step 11. Gift עולות come only on חול המועד. עולת ראייה comes even on יום טוב, from חולין only. שלמי שמחה may come from מעשר. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about the חגיגה of the first day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: עולות brought for vows and donations may come on חול המועד, but not on יום טוב. The עולת ראייה comes even on יום טוב, and when it comes, it must come only from חולין. שלמי שמחה may come even from מעשר. About the חגיגה of the first day of פסח: בית שמאי say it must come from חולין, and בית הלל say it may come from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says, word for word, what it just said the משנה means. This supports its reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the גמרא filled in missing words in the משנה. Now it shows a ברייתא that already teaches that fuller version. So the reading from Step 11 is not just a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this. This phrase brings support from a ברייתא.
Vows and donations: offerings a person chooses to bring, not ones he is required to bring.
The required עולה brought when a person comes to the בית המקדש on the festival.
שלמים eaten to fulfill the מצוה of rejoicing on the festival.
Here it means מעשר שני money, which must be spent in ירושלים.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three different rules. Gift עולות: only on חול המועד. עולת ראייה: even on יום טוב, but from חולין. שלמי שמחה: may come from מעשר. On the חגיגה of the first day of פסח, בית שמאי say חולין and בית הלל say מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'when it comes, it comes only from חולין' is about the עולת ראייה alone. The שלמי שמחה in the next line are different and may come from מעשר.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
Burnt-offerings brought for vows and donations
may come on the intermediate days of the festival,
but on יום טוב they may not come.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה בָּאָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: And the burnt-offering of appearance comes even on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהִיא בָּאָה — אֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין.
phrases.english: And when it comes, it may come only from non-sacred money.

phrases.aramaic: וְשַׁלְמֵי שִׂמְחָה בָּאִין אַף מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: And peace-offerings of rejoicing may come even from the tithe.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲגִיגַת יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: And the festival offering of the first day of Pesach:
בית שמאי say: from non-sacred money,
and בית הלל say: from the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the filled-in reading of the משנה from Step 11 with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The גמרא's filled-in reading of the משנה from Step 11.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that teaches the same rules about gift עולות, עולת ראייה, שלמי שמחה, and the חגיגה of פסח.

steps.title: Why does it say 'the first day of פסח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא names the חגיגה of the first day of פסח in particular.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the חגיגה of the first day of פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא names one exact day. It asks what that detail is there to teach. This question sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every festival has a חגיגה, so naming the first day of פסח looks extra. The גמרא assumes each word teaches something, so it asks what this detail adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why one case is treated or worded differently.
The festival peace-offering a person brings on the festival.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא חֲגִיגַת יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח?
phrases.english: What is different about the festival offering of the first day of Pesach?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא חֲגִיגַת יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about one specific detail in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא names the חגיגה of the first day of פסח in particular.

steps.title: רב אשי: the fifteenth is included, the fourteenth is not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains why the day is named. The ruling covers the חגיגה of the fifteenth of ניסן, but not the חגיגה brought on the fourteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This teaches us something. The חגיגה of the fifteenth is included, yes. The חגיגה of the fourteenth is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from Step 13. Naming the first day of פסח limits the ruling to the חגיגה of the fifteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is also a חגיגה brought on the fourteenth, together with the קרבן פסח. By naming the fifteenth, the text limits the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל to the חגיגה of the fifteenth. The חגיגה of the fourteenth is not part of their argument, and it is not an obligation, so it may be bought with מעשר money according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us. It shows the new point a detail adds.
The חגיגה brought on the fourteenth of ניסן, along with the קרבן פסח.
Yes / no.

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about the חגיגה of the fifteenth. Everyone agrees that the חגיגה of the fourteenth may come from מעשר money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two פסח חגיגות are not the same. One small word in the ברייתא separates them.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
This is what it teaches us:
the festival offering of the fifteenth, yes;
phrases.notes: The fifteenth of ניסן is the first day of פסח itself.

phrases.english: the festival offering of the fourteenth, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'first day of פסח' limit the ruling to the חגיגה of the fifteenth and leave out the חגיגה of the fourteenth.
